answers.answer: It is a condition on a particular use, not a general manufacturing requirement. It applies to occupying an approved child restraint system on board a U.S.-registered civil aircraft during movement on the surface, takeoff, and landing, provided the child is accompanied as specified and the operator complies with required securing/weight conditions; booster-type, vest- and harness-type, and lap held child restraints remain unapproved unless specifically excepted, and the section generally excludes operations under part 121, 125, or 135 and persons subject to § 91.105.
The source specifies that the seat must bear the label, but it does not identify the manufacturer as the entity legally mandated to perform the labeling action.

No. The restraint system must also meet additional requirements, including being furnished by the operator or an authorized person, having the child accompanied by an authorized adult, not being an unapproved booster, vest/harness, or lap-held restraint (unless excepted), and the operator properly securing the restraint to an approved forward-facing seat/berth, properly securing the child within specified weight limits, and ensuring the system bears the appropriate label(s).
